programme.title: Die drei Leben der Clara Schumann
programme.desc: Die Biografie von Clara Schumann ist legendenumwoben: Ihre strenge Kindheit, ihr außergewöhnliches Talent als Pianistin, ihre frühe Liebe zum Komponisten Robert Schumann und die Erziehung von sieben Kindern bieten Material für Mythen und Klischees.

programme.title: Kammermusik von Mozart und Schostakowitsch
programme.desc: Der Geiger Renaud Capuçon tritt beim Festival Les Coups de Cœur de Chantilly auf und spielt Kammermusik aus dem klassischen Repertoire und dem Repertoire des 20. Jahrhunderts. Er tritt mit den Solisten der Internationalen Menuhin-Musikakademie auf.

programme.title: Schumann - Fantasiestücke, Op.12
programme.desc: In dieser Aufführung vom Verbier Festival von 2018 zollt Seong-Jin Cho Claude Debussy Tribut anlässlich seines 100. Geburtstags. Auf dem Programm stehen Schumanns Fantasiestücke op. 12, die nur selten in Konzertprogrammen zu hören sind.

programme.title: Classica Spotlight
programme.desc: Filmische klassische Clips und energiegeladene Konzertstücke mit aufstrebenden Künstlern.

programme.title: Bach - Goldberg-Variationen, BWV 988
programme.desc: Der italienische Pianist Andrea Bacchetti spielt 2015 im Theater Carlo Felice in Genua Bachs Goldberg-Variationen, BWV 988. Das Werk ist nach dem Cembalisten Johann Gottlieb Goldberg benannt, der möglicherweise der erste Interpret des Werkes war.

programme.title: Sol Gabetta auf dem Lucerne Festival 2018
programme.desc: Die argentinische Cellistin Sol Gabetta kehrte 2018 zum Lucerne Festival zurück, um gemeinsam mit dem Mahler Chamber Orchestra unter der Leitung des Dirigenten François-Xavier Roth ein Konzert zu geben.

programme.title: Sinding - Serenade in A-Dur, Op. 92
programme.desc: Francesca Dego und Domenico Nordio sowie Andrea Bacchetti spielen die Serenade in A-Dur, Op. 92 des norwegischen Komponisten Christian Sinding. Diese Aufführung wurde am 2. Dezember 2013 im Teatro Comunale Città di Vicenza, Italien, aufgenommen.

programme.title: In der Probe: - Mariss Jansons
programme.desc: Mariss Jansons probt mit dem Oslo Philharmonischen Orchester die kraftvolle Suite aus Béla Bartóks Pantomimenballett "Der wunderbare Mandarin", gefolgt von einer Aufführung des gleichen Stücks aus dem Konzerthaus von Oslo.

programme.title: Schubert -- Rondo D. 951
programme.desc: Anlässlich ihres 80. Geburtstags widmete sich die argentinische Pianistin Martha Argerich der Kammermusik. Auf dem Programm standen unter anderem Felix Mendelssohns Klaviertrio Nr. 1 in d-Moll, Op. 49 und Franz Schuberts Rondo in A-Dur, D. 951.

programme.title: Classica Spotlight
programme.desc: Filmische klassische Clips und energiegeladene Konzertstücke mit aufstrebenden Künstlern.

programme.title: In the Organ's Stomach
programme.desc: Olivier Latry, der aktuelle Titularorganist der großen Orgel von Notre-Dame, führt die Zuschauer mit seinem Instrument auf eine Reise durch Landschaften, die Geschichte und unglaubliche Abenteuer, deren Zeuge das Instrument war.

programme.title: Chopin - Introduktion und Polonaise, Op. 3
programme.desc: Die Cellistin Silvia Chiesa und der Pianist Maurizio Baglini spielen Frédéric Chopins Introduction und Polonaise brillante in C-Dur, Op. 3. Das Konzert wurde 2024 im Sala Verdi des Conservatorio Giuseppe Verdi in Mailand aufgenommen.

programme.title: Mahler - Sinfonie Nr. 1 in D-Dur, 'Titan'
programme.desc: Das Maggio Musicale Fiorentino ist das älteste Opernfestival Italiens. Der Maestro Daniel Harding übernimmt das Dirigieren in einem wunderbaren Konzertprogramm mit der tragischen Ouvertüre in d-Moll, Op. 81 von Johannes Brahms.

programme.title: Werke von Gluck, Bach und Mozart
programme.desc: Der in Venezuela geborene Dirigent Giovanni Guzzo leitet durch dieses 2024 in Madrid aufgezeichnete Konzert. Es standen Werke von Christoph Willibald Gluck, Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart und Johann Sebastian Bach auf dem Programm.

programme.title: Beethoven - Letzte Sonate Op. 109, 110 & 111
programme.desc: Seine drei letzten Sonaten widmet Beethoven den intimen Dynamiken der menschlichen Seele, die von Verzweiflung bis Verwandlung reichen. Im Film werden die Musikwerke mit Szenen in verlassenen Schlössern untermalt, die an Einsamkeit erinnern.

programme.title: Beethoven - Sinfonie Nr. 9 in d-Moll, op. 125
programme.desc: Das Orchester de l'Opéra national de Paris unter Leitung von Philippe Jordan interpretiert die neunte Symphonie von Ludwig van Beethoven. Die Solisten sind Ricarda Merbeth, Daniela Sindram, Robert Dean Smith und Günther Groissböck.

programme.title: Mahler - Das Lied von der Erde
programme.desc: Die Mezzosopranistin Magdalena Kožená und der Tenor Andrew Staples schließen sich Sir Simon Rattle an, um den Zyklus "Das Lied von der Erde" von Gustav Mahler zu Gehör zu bringen. Das Konzert fand am 9. Mai 2021 im Barbican Centre in London statt.

programme.title: Mahler - Symphonie Nr. 7
programme.desc: Ungewöhnliche Orchesterfarben und -effekte. Die Verwendung seltenerer Instrumente und die frischen Klanglandschaften, die Mahler schafft, führen zu einem reichen und einzigartigen Hörerlebnis.

programme.title: Grieg - Klavierkonzert in a-Moll, Op. 16
programme.desc: Dirigent Jan Latham-Koenig leitet das Flanders Symphony Orchestra mit einer Aufführung von Edvard Griegs Klavierkonzert in a-Moll, Op. 16. Diese Aufführung wurde am 21. April 2016 im Concertgebouw Brügge, Belgien, aufgezeichnet.

programme.title: Rachmaninow und Gershwin: Rhapsodies
programme.desc: Das National Philharmonic Orchestra of Russia unter der Leitung von Dirigent Konstantin Kwatinets präsentiert Werke von Rachmaninow und George Gershwin. Der gefeierte russische Pianist Boris Berezowski ist ebenfalls mit von der Partie.

programme.title: Werke von Bach, Bartók und Brahms
programme.desc: Iván Fischer führt sein Budapest Festival Orchester mit Werken von Johann Sebastian Bach, Béla Bartók und Johannes Brahms. Die Aufführung wurde am 4. Dezember 2017 in der Béla Bartók National Concert Hall in Budapest aufgezeichnet.

programme.title: Verdi - Nabucco
programme.desc: Das Orchester der Arena di Verona interpretiert Giuseppe Verdis dritte Oper „Nabucco" unter der Leitung des israelischen Dirigenten Daniel Oren. Das erfolgreiche Werk feierte seine Uraufführung im Jahr 1842 im Teatro alla Scala in Mailand.

programme.title: Martinů - Concertino für Klaviertrio & orchester
programme.desc: Das italienisch-schweizerische Ensemble Trio des Alpen und das Orchestra da Camera di Mantova führen das Concertino für Klaviertrio und Streichorchester von Bohuslav Martinů auf. Diese Aufführung wurde 2016 im Teatro Bibiena in Mantua aufgenommen.

programme.title: True History
programme.desc: (Special, Documentary) - 2022-01-01

programme.title: The American Civil War - The Lower South Secedes
programme.desc: Beginning with South Carolina in December 1860, all the Lower South states secede by the first week of February 1861; they send delegates to a convention in Montgomery, Alabama, that establishes the Confederate States of America.

programme.title: The American Civil War - The Crisis at Fort Sumter
programme.desc: From February through April 1861, the United States and the Confederacy eye each other warily and vie for the support of eight slave states; as various compromise proposals fall short, Fort Sumter in Charleston Harbor becomes a flashpoint.

programme.title: The American Civil War - The Opposing Sides, I
programme.desc: Many think that the South is fated to lose; learning when the Confederate States of America came closest to winning; as fighting begins, each side has important advantages.

programme.title: The American Civil War - The Opposing Sides, II
programme.desc: Learning whether the Confederacy has better generals and which side has the edge in strategic and political leadership; the attitudes of England and France; studying the side which marshals its resources and exploits its advantages more effectively.

programme.title: The American Civil War - The Common Soldier
programme.desc: Learning why the young men join the colors of the North or the South; understanding what makes them bear the war's awful dangers and hardships; uncovering what it is like to be a soldier in the ranks.

programme.title: The American Civil War - First Manassas or Bull Run
programme.desc: Following the Upper South's secession and the move of the Confederate capital to Richmond, Virginia, both sides gear up for war; learning the details of General Winfield Scott's Anaconda Plan and the factors that lead to the Battle of First Manassas.

programme.title: The Great Tours: Civil War Battlefields - The Power of Place: The Civil War in Context
programme.desc: Exploring the significance of battlefields and the methods employed by soldiers in combat.

programme.title: The Great Tours: Civil War Battlefields - Manassas: The First Battle of Bull Run
programme.desc: Marching from Washington, Irvin McDowell's Union forces encounter P. G. T. Beauregard's Confederate troops at Virginia's Bull Run.

programme.title: The Great Tours: Civil War Battlefields - The Seven Days' Battles
programme.desc: Robert E. Lee's Army of Northern Virginia and George B. McClellan's Army of the Potomac write a blood-soaked chapter in American history and alter the trajectory of the Civil War.

programme.title: The Great Tours: Civil War Battlefields - A Return to Manassas: The Second Battle of Bull Run
programme.desc: In the Second Battle of Bull Run, lieutenants James Longstreet and Thomas Stonewall Jackson play a crucial role in securing victory for Robert E. Lee.

programme.title: The Great Tours: Civil War Battlefields - Antietam: America's Bloodiest Day
programme.desc: The diverse terrains hinder troop formations and make the soldiers vulnerable to attacks during the Antietam battle. This results in intense fighting and many casualties.

programme.title: The Great Tours: Civil War Battlefields - After Antietam: Photography and Medicine
programme.desc: The war photographers provide an up-close look at the devastation caused during the Antietam battle. Compassionate medics like Clara Barton go down in history as heroes.

programme.title: The Great Tours: Civil War Battlefields - The Battle of Fredericksburg
programme.desc: The politically driven decision to replace McClellan with Burnside leads the Union soldiers to their doom in Fredericksburg.

programme.title: The Great Tours: Civil War Battlefields - The Battle of Chancellorsville
programme.desc: Victory comes at a heavy price for Robert E. Lee in the Battle of Chancellorsville after he employs some arguably high-risk battle strategies.

programme.title: Unsung Heroes of World War II: Europe - Andrée de Jongh and the Resistance
programme.desc: When the Germans begin their rapid invasions across Europe, many ordinary citizens are stunned; Dedee de Jongh, a 23-year-old nurse, builds an escape line through Belgium and France to rescue stranded British airmen; her courage and ingenuity.

programme.title: Unsung Heroes of World War II: Europe - The Tory Rebels Who Helped Save England
programme.desc: In hindsight, it may appear inevitable that Winston Churchill takes command; at the time, it seems unthinkable that Neville Chamberlain steps down; how a few brave politicians orchestrate one of the most striking political transitions in history.

programme.title: Unsung Heroes of World War II: Europe - Victor de Laveleye and V for Victory
programme.desc: As an Olympic athlete, Victor de Laveleye is not an ordinary man; there is no reason to think he comes up with one of the war's most popular symbols, helping to buoy spirits and wage psychological warfare; the story of the V for Victory campaign.

programme.title: Unsung Heroes of World War II: Europe - Wilhelmina and Haakon: Royalty Fight Back
programme.desc: When the Germans invade the Netherlands and Norway, Adolf Hitler wants to secure the leadership of these nations; the wrenching decisions and harrowing escapes of Queen Wilhelmina and King Haakon; how these royal figures fight the war from Britain.

programme.title: Unsung Heroes of World War II: Europe - Polish Pilots and the Battle of Britain
programme.desc: The RAF's air battle to defend Britain from Germany in 1940; few people know that roughly 20 percent of the RAF consists of non-British pilots; witnessing the courage and successful maneuvers of Polish fighter pilots who save the day.

programme.title: Unsung Heroes of World War II: Europe - Wendell Willkie: \"A Godsend to This Country\"
programme.desc: It might seem impossible to find a politician willing to sabotage his own campaign; that is exactly what Wendell Willkie does in his 1940 run against President Roosevelt: why he goes against his own party and supports FDR's plans to help Britain.

programme.title: Unsung Heroes of World War II: Europe - The Earl of Suffolk and Heavy Water
programme.desc: Charles Henry George Howard, the 20th Earl of Suffolk, is an Englishman who seems unlikely to be responsible for the future of the free world; how he smuggles French scientists to England; how he foils Nazi efforts to obtain a nuclear bomb.

programme.title: Unsung Heroes of World War II: Europe - Marie-Madeleine Fourcade: Spymaster
programme.desc: For years, the history books suggest there are no women leaders of the Resistance in France; the story of Marie-Madeleine Fourcade blows this theory out of the water; meeting this extraordinary woman; how she leads a spy ring throughout France.

programme.title: The Vietnam War - America Enters the War
programme.desc: U.S. Marines arrive in June 1965 to protect a U.S. air base; the North Vietnamese Army and the southern Viet Cong guerrillas launch attacks.

programme.title: The Vietnam War - French Indochina and the Viet Minh
programme.desc: Surveying the economic exploitation and repression that defines Vietnam in the 19th and early 20th centuries.

programme.title: The Vietnam War - Dien Bien Phu and Vietnam Divided, 1953-1959
programme.desc: Examining mid-century Vietnam from the First Indochina War to the October 1955 referendum.

programme.title: The Vietnam War - Five Leaders Who Defined the Vietnam War
programme.desc: Explore the makings of war in Vietnam through five major players, starting with Vietnamese leaders Hồ Chí Minh and Lê Duẩn in the north and Ngo Dinh Diem in the south.

programme.title: The Vietnam War - The Rise of the Viet Cong, 1959-1962
programme.desc: Examining why the northern Vietnamese government decided to wage guerilla war in the south, and how it's adversaries responded.

programme.title: The Vietnam War - South Vietnam in Crisis, 1963
programme.desc: In 1963, South Vietnam careens toward crisis; exploring the ARVN's deficiencies from lackluster military commanders to political legitimacy.

programme.title: The Vietnam War - The Gulf of Tonkin and a Crossroads, 1964
programme.desc: Examining how the specter of communism in neighboring Indonesia shaped calculations made by the United States.

programme.title: The Vietnam War - The Vietnam War in the Skies
programme.desc: While the United States boasts an impressive air force, its air campaign struggles when confronted by VC forces.

programme.title: American Military History: From Colonials to Counterinsurgents - America: Forged in War
programme.desc: Exploring The French and Indian War of the mid-1700s, which is one of the formative conflicts in American military history; focusing on the experiences of Lt. Col. George Washington, a young colonial officer fighting for the British.

programme.title: American Military History: From Colonials to Counterinsurgents - George Washington Takes Command
programme.desc: When the colonies begin their struggle for independence, they choose George Washington to lead the army; Washington's defense of Boston; his defeat trying to hold New York City; contrasting British and American objectives in the Revolutionary War.

programme.title: American Military History: From Colonials to Counterinsurgents - Redcoats Fall to the Continental Army
programme.desc: Washington's army is in dire straits; his command is in question; he revives his reputation with the famous crossing of the Delaware River; the next four years of the American Revolution, which see Britain's strategic advantage deteriorate.

programme.title: American Military History: From Colonials to Counterinsurgents - Andrew Jackson and the War of 1812
programme.desc: Why the United States chooses to fight Britain in the War of 1812; America's grievances and ambitions, which include the conquest of Canada; the poor strategy, command and training that lead to a strategic stalemate; the exception is Andrew Jackson.

programme.title: American Military History: From Colonials to Counterinsurgents - The Mexican-American War of 1846-1848
programme.desc: The continental U.S. reaches its present span due to the Mexican-American War; the strategies and tactics of generals Zachary Taylor and Winfield Scott; what disciplined and bold maneuvers conducted by a professional army can accomplish.

programme.title: American Military History: From Colonials to Counterinsurgents - Opening Volleys of the Civil War: 1861-1862
programme.desc: The Civil War sets the pattern for warfare in the 20th and 21st centuries; the political events leading up to the war; the strategy devised by Winfield Scott; the chaotic First Battle of Bull Run; developments in the western theater.

programme.title: American Military History: From Colonials to Counterinsurgents - The Civil War's Main Front: 1862
programme.desc: The ebb and flow of battle in the eastern theater; President Lincoln promotes and fires top commanders; The South faces instability in its top ranks until Robert E. Lee becomes the Rebel army's leader; following events through the Battle of Antietam.

programme.title: American Military History: From Colonials to Counterinsurgents - Vicksburg to Gettysburg: 1862-1863
programme.desc: In the summer of 1863, the Civil War reaches a climax on two fronts; studying the generalship of Grant in isolating and defeating the Confederate force defending Vicksburg; dissecting Gen. George Meade's tactics that halt Lee's invasion of the North.

programme.title: The Real History of Pirates - What is a Pirate?
programme.desc: Exploring the reasons piracy endures from ancient times until today; why it is so difficult to both define and eradicate; how one can understand the rule of law and the rights of nations and individuals on the high seas and in borderless realms.

programme.title: The Real History of Pirates - Pirate Facts and Fictions
programme.desc: Examining popular pirate legends; discovering which aspects include some truth and which contain none at all; pirate literature can teach a lot about the Jolly Roger, gold-filled treasure chests, the pirate Edward Thatch and more.

programme.title: The Real History of Pirates - Real Pirates of the Caribbean
programme.desc: How the Spanish's power hold on the Caribbean is broken; which nationalities join in the free-for-all; the historical importance of Alexander Exquemelin's "Buccaneers of America" and Captain Charles Johnson's "A General History of the Pyrates".

programme.title: The Real History of Pirates - Pirate Attacks and Tactics
programme.desc: Pirates want money or anything they can turn into money; consequently, they usually wish for a speedy surrender, do not want a battle and rarely sink captured ships; the many tactics pirates use to apprehend their prey in the age of sails.

programme.title: The FBI Files
programme.desc: In Kokomo, Indiana an unthinkable crime terrified residents. A young woman was snatched from her home on a bright spring morning. Drops of blood and a torn window screen were all that was left to tell authorities what happened to the twenty-one year old victim. After several days of searching, a former FBI profiler narrowed the suspect list to one. Agents and detectives followed the trail across state lines hoping to find the victim before her time ran out.

programme.title: The FBI Files
programme.desc: In July 1997, a triple murder terrified residents in the nation's capital. In a Georgetown coffee shop, three employees were shot to death. Investigators could find no immediate suspects and no clear motive for the attack. Evidence at the crime scene pointed in many different directions. Was this a hate crime, a robbery gone wrong, or an act of cold-blooded vengeance against one of the victims?

programme.title: The FBI Files
programme.desc: In 1986, a small crime free Indiana town was turned inside out by the arrival of one dangerous stranger. After an officer was gunned down at point-blank range, the psychotic killer led investigators across the Midwest. No one knew where the gunman would strike next, even as his tally of murders and abductions grew. The FBI and state police raced against time to rescue America's heartland from this deranged gunman, before he killed again.

programme.title: The FBI Files
programme.desc: In Langley, Virginia, a gunman fired into rush hour traffic. The brazen daytime shooting of employees from the Central Intelligence Agency stunned the country. The victims seemed randomly selected, but the motive appeared to be political. The FBI was called in, but the nationwide search quickly became a far-reaching international manhunt. Agents processed more than 2000 leads and crossed an ocean in the effort to deliver justice.

programme.title: The FBI Files
programme.desc: On the day before Thanksgiving, a mother discovered her 10 year-old son was missing from his school. No one knew how it could have happened. Within hours, the boy's entire family was frantically searching for him. The few leads in the case quickly turned cold and the FBI was called in to aid in the investigation. The search by agents and local authorities would cover a thousand miles to expose the kidnapper and find the missing child.

programme.title: The FBI Files
programme.desc: On a summer afternoon in upscale Lodi, California, a 12-year-old girl is abducted from her home. Scores of police officers and FBI agents converge, determined to find the young girl before it is too late. When the kidnapper's car is discovered in a field near Lodi, police dogs, helicopters, and hundreds of volunteers are employed in a round-the-clock search. It would take a community united in concern for one of their youngest to find the missing child.

programme.title: The FBI Files
programme.desc: In rural Texas, 13-year-old is kidnapped on her way to school. Frantic to find her safely, her millionaire father calls local authorities and the FBI. As police officers and agents conduct aerial surveillance, the father drives hundreds of miles through the night to deliver the ransom cash to a drop that the kidnappers keep changing. In a final effort to save the young girl, investigators must engage in a dangerous firefight with five desperate criminals.

programme.title: The FBI Files
programme.desc: In September 1997, a team of masked gunmen robbed an armored car facility in Los Angeles, and made off with $18.9 million, the largest takeover heist in U.S. history. An employee believed she recognized the voice of one of the robbers, and FBI agents began conducting surveillance on a former employee of the facility. With only one piece of physical evidence, a fragment of a vehicle taillight, authorities hoped to connect him to the crime, and locate his accomplices.

programme.title: The FBI Files
programme.desc: In July 1996, two men entered a pawnshop in Birmingham, Alabama, and ruthlessly murdered the employees. Unbeknownst to the killers, a secret video surveillance camera recorded the shooting. Local police and the FBI released images of the crime to the media, and were quickly able to identify the perpetrators. Now authorities had to find two cold-blooded killers who knew that they were being pursued for murder one.

programme.title: The FBI Files
programme.desc: In Lincoln County, Nebraska, a fugitive drug dealer engaged in a shootout with state troopers, wounding two of them, and eluded capture after a high-speed chase. Authorities immediately set up a statewide manhunt, connecting the fugitive to a murder in western Nebraska. A chance sighting led FBI agents to a second confrontation with the killer, who was more determined than ever to escape the law.

programme.title: The FBI Files
programme.desc: After a career criminal committed a vehicular homicide in New Orleans, FBI agents tracked him through his habits and addictions. They focused their investigation on gambling communities throughout the country and, when he resurfaced in Atlantic City, authorities used all of their resources to trap an elusive sociopath who claimed that he would never be taken alive.

programme.title: The FBI Files
programme.desc: In the early 1980's, a pair of serial bank robbers gained a reputation among law enforcement officials as formidable bandits. Using the same modus operandi, the two men took hostages and emptied bank vaults across the Midwest. After the criminals escaped from police custody, FBI agents familiar with the bandits believed that they would attempt a grand-scale heist. By conducting surveillance on known associates of the criminals, authorities tried to anticipate the next target.

programme.title: The FBI Files
programme.desc: In the summer of 1999, Texas was terrorized by a brutal serial killer who traveled by train. The FBI assembled a task force to gather information about the dangerous drifter and create a profile that would help locate him. As they learned that the killer had traveled extensively through the United States and Mexico, the murders became more frequent, and authorities had to cast a dragnet over an entire continent in an effort to catch him.

programme.title: The FBI Files
programme.desc: On October 2, 1987, a Boston police officer responding to a domestic disturbance call was fatally wounded. Local authorities launched a citywide manhunt, but were only able to find the fingerprints of the chief suspect. Believing that he had fled the area, the FBI followed the suspect's trail to the west coast and then across the Mexican border, always aware of the desperation of a cop killer and of the need for justice.

programme.title: The FBI Files
programme.desc: In August 1984, the son of a successful real estate developer was kidnapped in front of his father's business in Miami. After the father received a $3 million ransom demand from a self-proclaimed terrorist, the FBI became involved. Based on witness descriptions of the car used in the kidnapping, authorities began to suspect a pair of Colombian nationals with a known grudge against the developer's family.

programme.title: The FBI Files
programme.desc: In October 1995, a South Carolina family was taken hostage as part of an elaborately planned bank robbery. Local police quickly identified two of the perpetrators, but the criminal mastermind proved more elusive. After his escape from custody, authorities began to suspect the fugitive of involvement in a series of bank robberies up and down the east coast, and the FBI remained on his trail, hoping to catch him before he took more hostages.

programme.title: The FBI Files
programme.desc: In February 1988, a record store clerk in Sandusky, Ohio, was fatally shot in his van. After discovering a night deposit bag with thousands of dollars in the vehicle, police knew that robbery was not the motive, and began to investigate other possibilities. FBI agents learned that several motorcycle gang members had been stopped nearby on a traffic violation shortly after the murder and theorized that the clerk's murder may have been a botched hit carried out by a gang member.

programme.title: The FBI Files
programme.desc: In June 1973, a young girl was abducted from a state park on the Missouri River while camping with her family. Several months passed with no leads, then an FBI agent took a particular interest in the case. Using a new technique known as criminal profiling, he predicted that the kidnapper would contact the girl's family on the one-year anniversary of her abduction. When this prediction came true, the FBI agent noted behavioral clues, hoping that they could lead him to the kidnapper.

programme.title: The FBI Files
programme.desc: In 1996, a group of political extremists twice robbed a bank in Spokane, Washington, using homemade bombs and military precision to escape. The FBI learned that the robbers, part of a shadowy organization called the Phineas Priesthood, might be preparing for a small-scale war with law enforcement. After the suspects were identified, the FBI was faced with the task of safely arresting a group of terrorists with a deadly agenda.

programme.title: The FBI Files
programme.desc: In August 1992, a man returned to his Memphis home and discovered that his wife was missing. The husband, as well as his friends, family and neighbors began to receive ransom calls. FBI agents noticed that one neighbor seemed to have the best rapport with the kidnapper. They began to question his level of involvement, but had to proceed carefully, knowing that he could be their only link to the missing woman.

programme.title: The FBI Files
programme.desc: In 1990 and 1991, Chicago police and the FBI were on the trail of a bank robber whose holdups were becoming increasingly violent. The criminal consistently used stolen Japanese cars to carry out the robberies, so authorities hoped to identify him by tracking vehicle thefts. When they finally located the man known as the bearded bandit, they learned that he did not work alone and he had made a pact never to surrender.

programme.title: The FBI Files
programme.desc: In 1988, new light was shed on the mysterious death of a South Carolina farmer when a criminal confessed that two prominent community members hired him to commit murder. Local police and FBI agents arrested a wealthy businessman and later learned that, even behind bars, he commanded the power to corrupt and kill. Using prison informants, agents had to prevent him from murdering again.

programme.title: The FBI Files
programme.desc: In October 1993, a robber surprised unsuspecting customers by dropping through the roof of a California bank. When police arrived, he escaped from the roof in a hail of bullets. A tip from a local resident led police and FBI agents to the perpetrator. They would soon learn that he had masterminded a local kidnapping, and held the fate of an innocent woman in his hands.
